paragraphs: We are a U.S.-based provider of advanced all-domain drone and robotic solutions for defense, national security, and commercial applications. We develop American-made hardware and software that supports military, government, and public safety operations across air, land, and sea. Our family of systems delivers tactical capabilities in small, unmanned aircraft systems (sUAS) and uncrewed surface vessels (USVs), delivering integrated platforms designed to enhance safety and multi-domain mission effectiveness.

We were originally incorporated under the laws of the State of Colorado in 1984 under the name Oravest International, Inc. In November 2016, we changed our name to TimefireVR, Inc. and re-incorporated in Nevada. In May 2019, the Company completed a share exchange agreement with Propware which resulted in the Propware shareholders acquiring an 83% ownership interest, and management control, of the Company. In connection with the share exchange agreement, we changed our name to Red Cat Holdings, Inc. ("Red Cat" or the "Company" or "we"). Following the share exchange agreement and our name change, we completed a series of acquisitions and financings which have broadened the scope of our activities in the drone industry.

The drone industry continues to expand to become a powerful business tool and recreational activity, with growth occurring broadly and across our targeted industries. Unmanned systems have become an increasingly important component of modern military operations. Unmanned aerial systems, as well as unmanned surface vessels, enable military forces to conduct intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, target acquisition, electronic warfare, and strike missions while reducing risk to personnel.

Advances in autonomy, sensors, communications, and artificial intelligence have expanded the operational capabilities of these systems and broadened the range of missions they can support. Compared to traditional manned platforms, many unmanned systems can be deployed more rapidly, operate in high-risk or contested environments, and be procured at significantly lower cost.

Recent conflicts have further demonstrated the operational effectiveness of relatively low-cost unmanned systems in areas including battlefield intelligence, force protection, and precision targeting. As a result, military organizations are increasingly integrating unmanned platforms into tactical units and broader operational planning. Many defense planners view unmanned systems as a force multiplier that can complement or augment conventional platforms across air, land, and maritime domains.

Demand for unmanned systems is supported by increasing global defense spending and evolving military modernization priorities. Governments worldwide continue to invest in advanced technologies intended to enhance military readiness, improve operational effectiveness, and maintain technological advantages in areas including autonomy, artificial intelligence, and networked systems.

In the United States, the Department of War ("DoW") has identified autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, and advanced sensing capabilities as key priorities within its broader modernization strategy. Multiple branches of the U.S. military have initiated programs focused on expanding the deployment of tactical unmanned systems, including small drones designed to support frontline units with real-time intelligence and situational awareness.

On November 5, 2024, the U.S. Presidential and Congressional elections occurred, with Donald Trump being elected President of the United States, and the Republican party controlling both the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives. On March 14, 2025 the Senate voted to pass the "Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act of 2025" (H.R. 1968) to further extend appropriations and avert a government shutdown through the end of the federal government's fiscal year 2025 on September 30, 2025. This continuing resolution ("CRA") largely extended fiscal year 2024 spending levels, including certain limited flexibility to reallocate certain program funds, and, according to the Congressional Budget Office, would allow for $1.6 trillion in discretionary spending in the federal government's fiscal
year 2025, with $893 billion for defense (an approximately $6 billion increase) and $708 billion for non-defense spending (an approximately $13 billion reduction).

On July 4, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) was enacted. This reconciliation bill appropriated an additional $156 billion for defense spending and national security priorities and is expected to result in increased investment by the DoW in defense modernization projects and increasing weapons and armaments production capacity. Approximately $113 billion of the $156 billion in OBBBA funding for defense and national security priorities is intended to be added to the final 2026 defense appropriations bill (see below) The appropriated funds will remain available to be obligated until September 30, 2029 and can be expended through 2035.

The federal government's 2026 fiscal year began on October 1, 2025, without the passage of Appropriation Acts or a CRA, resulting in a U.S. Government shutdown. On November 9, 2025, a stopgap spending measure was enacted, which expired on January 30, 2026.

The U.S. Department of War's Fiscal Year 2026 budget request totals approximately $961.6 billion, which represents $843.3 billion in base budget (discretionary) and $113.3 billion in reconciliations (mandatory) funding, representing a continuation of the sustained increase in U.S. defense spending and reflecting ongoing investments in advanced technologies including autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and counter-unmanned aerial capabilities.

The potential challenges presented by the recent U.S. Government shutdown, Presidential and Congressional changes, proposed new tariffs, the current budgetary and deficit funding environment, the Trump Administration's stated fiscal policies, Israel, Ukraine, Venezuela and Taiwan funding support, potential heightened levels of inflation, ongoing supply chain disruption, and the challenging appropriations process, among other items, all continue to potentially create significant short and long-term risks to the industry and the Company. Additionally, the Trump Administration has recently executed certain executive orders directly related to significantly changing the current DoW procurement policies and procedures, and the Federal Acquisition Regulations, the potential impact of which such changes, if effected either by executive orders or changes to the relevant law, to the industry, are unknown at this time.

We believe however that our business is well-positioned, including in areas that the Trump Administration, the DoW, the FCC and national security related and other customers currently indicate are priorities for future defense spending. As noted above, we believe that there is a generational recapitalization of weapon systems and the defense industrial base occurring with the U.S. and its allies to address peer and near peer threats, including Russia, China, North Korea and Iran. We believe that our positioning as a proven provider of military grade hardware, products, systems and software to address these threats for and with our customers and partners is recognized in the industry.

We have incurred net losses since inception.
We may need additional capital to fund our expanding operations until we reach profitability, and if we are not able to obtain sufficient capital, we may be forced to limit or curtail our operations.
Lack of long-term purchase orders and commitments from customers may lead to a rapid decline in sales.
Our products require a continuing investment in research and development, and may experience technical problems or delays, which could lead the business to fail.
The nature of our business involves significant risks and uncertainties that may not be covered by insurance or indemnity.
Product quality issues and a higher-than-expected number of warranty claims or returns could harm our business and operating results.
Our operating results may be adversely impacted by worldwide political, economic and public health uncertainties and specific conditions in the markets we address.
Acquisitions could divert the attention of key personnel, be difficult to integrate, dilute our existing stockholders and adversely impact our financial results.
Our failure to effectively manage growth could harm our business.
Our products are subject to lengthy development cycles.
We expect to incur substantial research and development costs related to identifying and commercializing new products and services which may never result in revenues.
Our operations may be adversely affected if we lose our rights under third-party technology licenses.
If our customers are not satisfied with our technical support, firmware or software updates, they may choose not to purchase our products which would adversely impact business and operating results.
Our use of open-source software could negatively affect our ability to sell our products and could subject us to possible litigation.
We must recruit and retain highly trained and experienced employees, especially engineers, in order to succeed in our business.
Our facilities and information systems and those of our key suppliers could be damaged as a result of disasters or unpredictable events which could have an adverse effect on our business operations.
We depend on third parties to provide integrated circuit chip sets and other critical components for use in our products.
We may be subject to litigation, legal proceedings, and class action claims that could adversely affect our business and financial condition.
Our financial success is dependent on contracts awarded through a lengthy, uncertain and competitive process.
We operate in an emerging and rapidly growing industry which makes it difficult to evaluate our current business and prospects.
We face competition from larger companies that have substantially greater resources which challenges our ability to establish market share, grow our business segments, and reach profitability.
Our business is dependent upon our ability to keep pace with the latest technological changes.
Cybersecurity risks could adversely affect our business and disrupt our operations.
U.S. government contracts are generally not fully funded at inception and may include provisions that are not favorable to us which could adversely impact our cash flows and results of operations.

The U.S. Government provides a significant portion of our revenue, and our business could be adversely affected by changes in the fiscal policies of the U.S. Government and other governmental entities.
Government contracts differ materially from standard commercial contracts, involve competitive bidding and may be subject to cancellation or delay without penalty.

paragraphs: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our audited consolidated financial statements and related notes and other financial data included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. In addition to our historical consolidated financial information, the following discussion contains forward-looking statements that reflect our plans, estimates, and beliefs. Our actual results could differ materially from those discussed in the forward-looking statements. For more information regarding forward-looking statements, please refer to the discussion above under the heading "Forward-Looking Statements."

In September 2024, our Board of Directors approved a change in fiscal year end from April 30 to December 31, effective as of December 31, 2024. In accordance with SEC regulations, our Consolidated Financial Statements are comprised of our Consolidated Balance Sheets as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 and our Consolidated Statements of Operations, Consolidated Statements of Stockholders' Equity, Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows for the year ended December 31, 2025, eight months ended December 31, 2024, and year ended April 30, 2024. As a result, this Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations is comparing our results of operations for the year ended December 31, 2025 with our results of operations for the eight month period ended December 31, 2024 and the year ended April 30, 2024.

In April 2025, we entered into a securities purchase agreement with certain institutional investors pursuant to which we issued and sold, in a registered direct offering, an aggregate of 4,724,412 shares of our common stock, par value $0.001 per share, at a price of $6.35 per share. The gross proceeds were approximately $30 million, before deducting the placement agents' fees and other offering expenses.

In June 2025, we entered into a securities purchase agreement with certain institutional investors pursuant to which we issued and sold, in a registered direct offering, an aggregate of 6,448,276 shares of our common stock, par value $0.001 per share, at a price of $7.25 per share. The gross proceeds were approximately $46.8 million, before deducting the placement agents' fees and other offering expenses.

In September 2025, we entered into an underwriting agreement with a certain institutional investor pursuant to which we issued and sold, in a registered direct offering, an aggregate of 15,625,000 shares of our common stock, par value $0.001 per share, at a price of $9.60 per share. We also granted the underwriters a thirty day option to purchase up to an additional 2,343,750 shares of common stock at the public offering price, which the underwriters exercised in full at closing. The gross proceeds were approximately $172.5 million, before deducting the underwriters' fees and other offering expenses.

Consolidated revenues totaled $40.7 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 (or the "2025 Period") compared to $4.9 million during the eight months ended December 31, 2024 (or the "Transition Period") and compared to $17.8 million during the year ended April 30, 2024 (or the "2024 Period"). This represents an increase of $35.8 million, or 739% compared to the Transition Period and an increase of $22.9 million, or 128% compared to the 2024 Period. The increase compared to both periods is attributable primarily to increased revenue associated with the commencement and scaling of drone deliveries to the U.S. Army under the SRR program.

Consolidated gross profit totaled $1.3 million during the 2025 Period compared to gross loss of $1.4 million during the Transition Period and gross profit of $3.7 million during the 2024 Period. This represents an increase of $2.7 million, or 195% compared to the Transition Period and a decrease of $2.4 million, or 65% compared to the 2024 Period. On a

percentage basis, gross profit was 3% during the 2025 Period compared to gross loss of 28% during the Transition Period and gross profit of 21% during the 2024 Period. Our manufacturing facility is currently operating below its designed production capacity. These lower production levels, combined with higher fixed overhead costs, have resulted in lower gross margins during the 2025 Period. As production volumes increase, we expect fixed overhead costs, including labor, to be allocated across a greater number of units, which is expected to reduce per-unit production costs and improve gross margins.

Research and development expenses totaled $17.9 million during the 2025 Period compared to $6.6 million during the Transition Period and $6.3 million during the 2024 period. This represents an increase of $11.3 million, or 171% compared to the Transition Period and an increase of $11.6 million, or 186% compared to the 2024 Period. The increase compared to both periods was attributable primarily to increased investment in research and development activities, including engineering personnel costs, prototype development, testing, and other expenses associated with the development of new and enhanced drone platforms and related technologies.

Sales and marketing costs totaled $13.1 million during the 2025 Period compared to $6.3 million during the Transition Period and $5.1 million during the 2024 Period. This represents an increase of $6.8 million, or 107% compared to the Transition Period and an increase of $8.0 million, or 158% compared to the 2024 Period. The increase compared to both periods was attributable primarily to higher payroll and related personnel costs associated with expanding our sales and marketing team to support increased business development and customer engagement activities.

General and administrative expenses totaled $36.9 million during the 2025 Period compared to $11.5 million during the Transition Period and $11.2 million during the 2024 Period. This represents an increase of $25.4 million, or 222% compared to the Transition Period and $25.7 million, or 229% compared to the 2024 Period. The increase compared to both periods was attributable primarily to higher payroll and related personnel costs resulting from increased headcount, as well as higher stock-based compensation expense. These increases reflect the expansion of our corporate, administrative, and compliance functions to support growth during the 2025 Period.

Other expense totaled $5.0 million during the 2025 Period compared to $17.8 million during the Transition Period and $2.2 million during the 2024 Period. This represents a decrease of $12.8 million or 72% compared to the Transition Period and an increase of $2.8 million, or 126% compared to the 2024 Period. During the 2025 Period, other expense consisted primarily of a fair value adjustment on convertible notes payable of $11.4 million, partially offset by a gain on extinguishment of convertible notes payable of $3.2 million and net interest income of $2.7 million. During the Transition Period, other expense consisted primarily of a fair value adjustment on convertible note payable of $13.1 million and a loss on sale of equity method investment of $4.0 million. During the 2024 Period, other expense consisted primarily of impairment on equity method investment of $11.4 million, partially offset by a gain of $9.6 million related to the divestiture of the Consumer segment.

Net loss from continuing operations totaled $72.1 million during the 2025 Period compared to $43.6 million during the Transition Period and $21.5 million during the 2024 period. This represents a decrease of $28.5 million, or 65% compared to the Transition Period and a decrease of $50.6 million, or 235% compared to the 2024 Period.

Net cash used in operating activities was $89.1 million during the 2025 Period compared to $20.5 million during the Transition Period and $17.7 million during the 2024 Period. This represents an increase of $68.6 million compared to the Transition Period and an increase of $71.4 million compared to the 2024 Period. The increase compared to both periods was attributable primarily to the increase in net loss during the 2025 period. Non-cash expenses totaled $20.5 million during the 2025 period, compared to $22.6 million during Transition Period and $8.5 million during the 2024 Period. Net cash used related to changes in operating assets and liabilities totaled $37.6 million during the 2025 Period. paragraphs: 本公司為美國境內提供先進全領域無人機與機械解決方案的供應商，應用於防衛、國家安全與商業用途。本公司開發美國製造的硬體與軟體，支援軍事、政府與公共安全作業，涵蓋空中、陸地與海上領域。本公司系統家族提供戰術能力，於小型無人機系統（sUAS）與無人水面載具（USVs）上，提供整合式平台，以提升安全與多領域任務效益。

本公司最初於科羅拉多州根據該州法律註冊成立，名為Oravest International, Inc.，於1984年成立。2016年11月，本公司更名為TimefireVR, Inc.，並重新註冊於內華達州。2019年5月，本公司完成與Propware的股票交換協議，導致Propware股東取得本公司83%的股權與管理控制權。根據股票交換協議，本公司更名為Red Cat Holdings, Inc.（"Red Cat" 或 "本公司" 或 "我們"）。在完成股票交換協議與更名後，本公司完成一系列收購與融資，擴大了本公司在無人機產業的業務範疇。
無人機產業持續擴張，成為強大商業工具與休閒活動，成長發生在廣泛且我們目標產業中。無人系統已成為現代軍事作戰的重要零組件。無人航空系統以及無人水面載具，使軍隊得以執行情報、監視與偵察、目標取得、電子戰與攻擊任務，同時降低人員風險。
自主性、感測器、通訊與人工智慧的進步，擴展了這些系統的作戰能力，並廣泛支持更多任務類型。與傳統有人平台相比，許多無人系統可更快速部署，執行高風險或爭議性環境作戰，且採購成本顯著較低。
近期衝突進一步顯示，相對低成本無人系統在戰場情報、部隊保護與精準目標等領域的作戰效益。因此，軍事組織正逐步將無人平台整合至戰術單位與更廣泛的作戰計畫中。許多防衛規劃者視無人系統為戰力倍增器，可在空中、陸地與海事領域補充或增強傳統平台。
對無人系統的需求受到全球防衛支出增加與軍事現代化優先順序變化的支撐。全球各國政府持續投資先進科技，以提升軍事作戰準備、改善作戰效益，並維持在自主性、人工智慧與網路系統等領域的科技優勢。
在美國，國防部（"DoW"）已將自主系統、人工智慧與先進感測能力識別為其廣泛現代化戰略中的關鍵優先事項。美國多個軍種已啟動專案，著重於擴展戰術無人系統的部署，包括小型無人機，以支援前線單位的即時情報與情境感知。

2024年11月5日，美國總統與國會選舉舉行，唐納·川普當選美國總統，共和黨控制美國參議院與眾議院。2025年3月14日，參議院投票通過「2025年全年持續撥款與延長法案」（H.R. 1968），以進一步延長撥款並避免政府停擺，直至2025年9月30日財政年度結束。此持續撥款法案（"CRA"）大致延續2024財年支出水平，包括某些有限的資金重新分配彈性，根據國會預算辦公室的資料，將允許美國政府2025財年有1.6兆美元的酌情支出。
2025 年，防禦支出為 893 十億美元（約增加 6 十億美元），非防禦支出為 708 十億美元（約減少 13 十億美元）。

2025 年 7 月 4 日，「One Big Beautiful Bill Act」（OBBBA）正式立法。此項協調法案為防禦支出與國家安全優先事項追加 156 十億美元經費，預期將導致 DoW 在防禦現代化專案上增加投資，並提高武器與裝備的生產能力。OBBBA 為防禦與國家安全優先事項追加的 156 十億美元經費中，約 113 十億美元預計將加入 2026 年防禦經費法案（詳見下文）。經費將自 2029 年 9 月 30 日前持續可用，並可於 2035 年前使用完畢。
美國聯邦政府 2026 財政年度於 2025 年 10 月 1 日開始，因未通過經費法案或 CRA，導致美國政府停擺。2025 年 11 月 9 日，通過臨時支出措施，該措施於 2026 年 1 月 30 日到期。
美國國防部 2026 財政年度預算請求總額約為 961.6 十億美元，包含 843.3 十億美元的基礎預算（自由裁量經費）與 113.3 十億美元的協調經費（義務經費），反映美國防禦支出持續增加，並反映對先進科技，包括自動化系統、人工智慧、網路安全及反無人機能力的持續投資。
近期美國政府停擺、總統與國會變動、新關稅提案、目前預算與赤字資金環境、特朗普政府所宣示的財政政策、以色列、烏克蘭、委內瑞拉與臺灣資金支持、潛在通貨膨脹升溫、供應鏈持續中斷，以及困難的經費審議程序等，皆持續可能對產業與本公司造成重大短期與長期風險。此外，特朗普政府近期已執行若干與大幅改變現行 DoW 財務採購政策與程序，以及聯邦採購規則相關的行政命令，這些變動對產業的潛在影響，目前尚無法預測。
然而，我們認為本公司業務處於優勢，包括特朗普政府、DoW、FCC 以及其他與國家安全相關的客戶目前所指明的未來防禦支出優先事項領域。如上所述，我們認為美國與其盟友正在進行一代的武器系統與防禦工業基礎的重組，以應對來自俄羅斯、中國、朝鮮與伊朗等對等與近對等威脅。我們相信本公司作為提供軍事級硬體、產品、系統與軟體的已驗證供應商，以應對這些威脅，並與客戶與合作夥伴共同作戰的定位，已為產業所認可。

paragraphs: 下列討論應與我們經審計之合併財務報表及相關附註，以及其他財務資料一併閱讀，此財務資料包含於本年度報告表 10-K 其他部分。除我們的歷史合併財務資訊外，下列討論包含向前看的陳述，反映我們的計畫、預估與信念。我們的實際結果可能與向前看陳述中所討論的有重大差異。如需更多有關向前看陳述的資訊，請參閱上述標題為「向前看陳述」的討論。

2024 年 9 月，我們董事會批准將會計年度結算日從 4 月 30 日改為 12 月 31 日，自 2024 年 12 月 31 日起生效。根據 SEC 規範，我們的合併財務報表包含我們截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日的合併資產負債表，以及 2025 年 12 月 31 日年度、2024 年 12 月 31 日八個月度及 2024 年 4 月 30 日年度的合併營業表現、合併股東權益變動表及合併現金流量表。因此，本管理層討論與分析財務狀況及營運成果，比較我們 2025 年 12 月 31 日年度營運成果與 2024 年 12 月 31 日八個月度及 2024 年 4 月 30 日年度營運成果。
2025 年 4 月，我們與某些機構投資者簽訂證券購買協議，根據協議，我們在註冊直接發行中發行並出售總計 4,724,412 股本公司普通股，每股票面價值 0.001 美元，每股價格為 6.35 美元。總計所得金額約為 30 百萬美元，扣除發行費用及中介費用前。
2025 年 6 月，我們與某些機構投資者簽訂證券購買協議，根據協議，我們在註冊直接發行中發行並出售總計 6,448,276 股本公司普通股，每股票面價值 0.001 美元，每股價格為 7.25 美元。總計所得金額約為 46.8 百萬美元，扣除發行費用及中介費用前。

2025 年 9 月，我們與某機構投資者簽訂承銷協議，根據協議，我們在註冊直接發行中發行並出售總計 15,625,000 股本公司普通股，每股票面價值 0.001 美元，每股價格為 9.60 美元。我們同時授予承銷商 30 天的選擇權，可購買最多 2,343,750 股普通股，以公開發行價格為基礎，承銷商在交割時已完全行使該選擇權。總計所得金額約為 172.5 百萬美元，扣除承銷商費用及發行費用前。

合併營收在 2025 年 12 月 31 日年度（簡稱「2025 期間」）總計為 40.7 百萬美元，較 2024 年 12 月 31 日八個月度（簡稱「過渡期間」）的 4.9 百萬美元，以及 2024 年 4 月 30 日年度（簡稱「2024 期間」）的 17.8 百萬美元有所增加。這代表與過渡期間相比，營收增加 35.8 百萬美元，或成長 739%，與 2024 期間相比，營收增加 22.9 百萬美元，或成長 128%。與兩個期間相比的成長，主要歸因於與美國陸軍 SRR 計畫相關的無人機配送業務啟動與擴張所帶來的營收增加。
合併毛利在 2025 期間總計為 1.3 百萬美元，較過渡期間的毛損 1.4 百萬美元，以及 2024 期間的毛利 3.7 百萬美元有所增加。這代表與過渡期間相比，毛利增加 2.7 百萬美元，或成長 195%，與 2024 期間相比，毛利減少 2.4 百萬美元，或下降 65%。以
百分比來看，毛利在 2025 期間為 3%，較過渡期間的毛損 28%，以及 2024 期間的毛利 21% 有所變化。我們的製造廠目前運作未達設計產能。這些較低的生產量，加上較高的固定間接費用，導致 2025 期間的毛利邊際較低。隨著生產量增加，我們預期固定間接費用，包括人工，將分配至更多單位，這預期會降低單位生產成本，並改善毛利邊際。
研究與開發費用於 2025 年期間合計為 17.9 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 6.6 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 6.3 百萬美元增加。此為較過渡期間增加 11.3 百萬美元，或 171%，較 2024 年期間增加 11.6 百萬美元，或 186%。與兩期間相比的增加，主要歸因於對研究與開發活動的投資增加，包括工程人員費用、原型開發、測試及其他與開發新產品及增強無人機平台及相關技術有關的費用。
銷售與行銷費用於 2025 年期間合計為 13.1 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 6.3 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 5.1 百萬美元增加。此為較過渡期間增加 6.8 百萬美元，或 107%，較 2024 年期間增加 8.0 百萬美元，或 158%。與兩期間相比的增加，主要歸因於因擴充銷售與行銷團隊以支持增加的業務開發及客戶互動活動而產生的較高薪資及相關人員費用。

一般及行政費用於 2025 年期間合計為 36.9 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 11.5 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 11.2 百萬美元增加。此為較過渡期間增加 25.4 百萬美元，或 222%，較 2024 年期間增加 25.7 百萬美元，或 229%。與兩期間相比的增加，主要歸因於因員工人數增加而產生的較高薪資及相關人員費用，以及較高的股票基於報酬費用。這些增加反映了我們在 2025 年期間擴充企業、行政及合規功能以支持成長。

其他費用於 2025 年期間合計為 5.0 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 17.8 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 2.2 百萬美元減少。此為較過渡期間減少 12.8 百萬美元，或 72%，較 2024 年期間增加 2.8 百萬美元，或 126%。於 2025 年期間，其他費用主要為可轉換票據應付帳款的公允價值調整 11.4 百萬美元，部分抵銷因可轉換票據應付帳款結清產生的收益 3.2 百萬美元及淨利息收入 2.7 百萬美元。於過渡期間，其他費用主要為可轉換票據應付帳款的公允價值調整 13.1 百萬美元及出售權益法投資產生的損失 4.0 百萬美元。於 2024 年期間，其他費用主要為權益法投資的減損 11.4 百萬美元，部分抵銷因出售消費部門產生的收益 9.6 百萬美元。
持續運營業務的淨虧損於 2025 年期間合計為 72.1 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 43.6 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 21.5 百萬美元減少。此為較過渡期間減少 28.5 百萬美元，或 65%，較 2024 年期間減少 50.6 百萬美元，或 235%。

營運活動所使用的淨現金為 89.1 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 20.5 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 17.7 百萬美元增加。此為較過渡期間增加 68.6 百萬美元，較 2024 年期間增加 71.4 百萬美元。與兩期間相比的增加，主要歸因於 2025 年期間淨虧損的增加。非現金費用於 2025 年期間合計為 20.5 百萬美元，較過渡期間的 22.6 百萬美元及 2024 年期間的 8.5 百萬美元增加。營運活動相關資產及負債變動所使用的淨現金於 2025 年期間合計為 37.6 百萬美元。營運活動相關資產及負債變動所產生的淨現金於過渡期間合計為 0.4 百萬美元。營運活動所使用的淨現金

我們自設立以來已產生淨虧損。
本公司可能需要額外資金以支應擴張營運至達成獲利，若無法取得足夠資金，可能被迫限制或縮減營運。
客戶長期採購訂單及承諾不足，可能導致銷售快速下滑。
本公司產品需要持續投入研究與開發經費，並可能遭遇技術問題或延誤，此情形可能導致業務失敗。
本公司業務性質涉及重大風險與不確定性，且可能未被保險或賠償條款所涵蓋。
產品品質問題及高於預期的保固申告或退貨數量，可能影響本公司業務與營運成果。
本公司營運成果可能因全球政治、經濟及公共衛生不確定性，以及所處市場特定條件而受到不利影響。
併購可能分散關鍵人員注意力、整合困難、稀釋現有股東權益，並對財務成果造成不利影響。
本公司若無法有效管理成長，可能對業務造成損害。
本公司產品面臨漫長的開發週期。
預期將產生大量研究與開發費用，用以識別及商業化新產品與服務，這些費用可能永遠無法產生收入。
若本公司喪失第三方技術授權之權利，將可能對營運產生不利影響。
若客戶對本公司之技術支援、固件或軟體更新不滿意，可能選擇不購買本公司產品，將對營業與營運成果產生不利影響。
本公司使用開放來源軟體可能對銷售產品產生負面影響，並可能使本公司面臨訴訟風險。
本公司必須招募並留住高素養與經驗豐富之員工，尤其是工程師，以成功經營本公司業務。
本公司廠房與資訊系統，以及關鍵供應商之廠房與資訊系統，可能因災難或無法預測之事件而受損，可能對本公司營運產生不利影響。
本公司依賴第三方提供用於產品之整合電路晶片組及其他關鍵零組件。
本公司可能涉及訴訟、法律程序及集體訴訟聲請，此等情事可能對本公司業務及財務狀況造成不利影響。
本公司財務表現取決於透過漫長、不確定且競爭激烈的程序所授予之契約。
本公司營運於一個新興且快速成長之產業，此等產業特性使評估本公司目前業務及前景變得困難。
本公司面臨來自規模較大之企業之競爭，這些企業擁有遠較本公司為之豐富之資源，此等競爭可能影響本公司建立市場佔有率、成長業務分部及達成獲利能力之能力。
本公司業務取決於本公司能否跟上最新之科技變革。
網路安全風險可能對本公司業務造成不利影響，並幹擾本公司營運。
美國政府契約通常在簽約時並未完全經費支應，且可能包含對本公司不利之條款，此等情事可能對本公司現金流及營運成果造成不利影響。
美國政府提供本公司相當大比例之營業收入，而本公司業務可能因美國政府及其它政府機構財政政策之變動而受到不利影響。
